focal_entities.audience: the user at the plan sign-off, approving what the finished work will do and why, and rn's orchestrator in any later conversation, carrying the work on without asking them again

goal_orientation.purpose: approving the goal and the acceptance criteria, then carrying each later work to them

goal_orientation.serves: G1: A first-time contributor learns they are welcome to try things freely here, so they find it easy to join in.
AC1: The README gains one line that tells a newcomer both that they are welcome and that they may try things freely, and its two existing lines stay as they are.

constraints.decision: What the greeting is for: A first-time contributor learns they are welcome to try things freely here, so they find it easy to join in

What shows it done: AC1: the README gains one line that tells a newcomer they are welcome and may try things freely and links to CONTRIBUTING.md, its two existing lines as they are; AC2: CONTRIBUTING.md says the two points alone
Tasks of the plan stage: The plan stage's tasks serve G1 and reach the acceptance criteria; adding the line to README.md is left to the build stage
How the goal's reason is checked: AC1 checks that the welcome and trying freely get across, and AC2 that a newcomer learns how to join in; together they check the goal, with no criterion added for it
Calls of a plan-stage task: A plan-stage task's design and making steps name work plan, kind plan, with no path, as rn's calls make the plan
How a task names what it serves: Each task line ends exactly "Serves <G1, or the criteria by ID>.", such as "Serves G1.", with nothing after it, as rn's scripts read it

Wording of AC1: AC1 says the one new README line welcomes a newcomer, says they may try things freely and links to CONTRIBUTING.md, the two existing lines unchanged; AC2 says CONTRIBUTING.md holds the two points alone
The CONTRIBUTING file: A short CONTRIBUTING.md is made, and the README's greeting line links to it, so a newcomer has somewhere real to read how to join in
What CONTRIBUTING.md says: CONTRIBUTING.md says two things alone: a newcomer may try things freely, and a change goes in by making a branch and opening a pull request

T1 after AC1 changed: T1 is opened again, unticked from step 2: its completion criterion and its checks cover AC1's link to CONTRIBUTING.md as well as the two points, so the new AC1 is checked before the sign-off
